headline_marked: Micron locks in [[historically high memory prices]] for five years
headline: Micron locks in historically high memory prices for five years
summary: Micron signs 16 strategic customer agreements with floor prices for high gross margins. The deals cover 40% of Micron's revenue.
details: Micron has signed 16 'strategic customer agreements' (SCAs) that include a floor price the company says comes with 'a very robust gross margin for Micron, well above our peak quarterly margins in any past cycle.' The agreements cover 2026 to 2030 and involve a commitment to buy a certain quantity of product and pay for it in a pricing band that has a floor and a ceiling price.

The CEO of Micron, Sanjay Mehrotra, explained that the SCAs will account for 40 percent of Micron revenue, meaning the company is reserving most of its inventory to sell at prices it can negotiate. Mehrotra also mentioned that customers are recognizing that supply shortages in memory and storage will take considerable time to improve.

Despite efforts to build new chip fabs, Mehrotra said the increasing complexity of new memory types means it takes longer to build factories. When they come online, there still won't be enough capacity to build both the high-bandwidth memory needed for AI and other types of NAND and DRAM.

Micron's revenue landed at $41.5 billion, a fifth consecutive quarterly revenue record and 346 percent year-over-year jump. DRAM revenue alone reached a record $31.3 billion, up 343 percent year-over-year.
